title: Le retour du passé  (The Return of the Past)

segments.t: Devastated to find a farewell note from Colette, Andrea heads straight to the film studio. On set, an enthusiastic Jose Garcia describes his passionate new role, before a sudden encounter with his former partner Laurence completely throws him off balance. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Colette m'a laissé un mot terrible.
Ce que tu fais est irresponsable!
Ça va être une bonne journée!
Ce nouveau rôle m'emballe vraiment.
Je vais donner envie de manger.
Tu as l'air bizarre ce matin.
C'est un peu tendu avec Colette.
Sans Colette, tu veux dire.
José? Comment tu vas?
Ça fait vraiment une éternité!
Je suis ravie d'être sur ce tournage.
À tout à l'heure sur le plateau.
Laurence... Que fait-elle ici?
Tu la connais depuis longtemps?
Let's explore this dramatic encounter line by line.
Colette m'a laissé un mot terrible.
'Colette left me a terrible note.' Andrea struggles to accept that Colette packed her bags and left. The verb meaning 'has' pairs naturally with the noun for 'note' in everyday conversation.
Ce que tu fais est irresponsable!
'What you are doing is irresponsible!' Andrea leaves an exasperated message on Colette's phone. The descriptive adjective for 'irresponsible' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
Ça va être une bonne journée!
'It is going to be a good day!' Jose welcomes his agent with cheerful optimism. French forms the near future by pairing the present tense of 'to go' directly with 'to be'.
Ce nouveau rôle m'emballe vraiment.
'This new role truly excites me.' Jose expresses deep enthusiasm for his creative performance. Notice how 'excites' leads directly into the noun meaning 'role'.
Je vais donner envie de manger.
'I will make people want to eat.' Jose describes how vibrant food preparation will bring the scene alive. French forms the near future by pairing the present tense of 'to go' directly with 'to eat'.
Tu as l'air bizarre ce matin.
'You look strange this morning.' Jose perceives Andrea's visible distress and lack of focus. The informal 'you' form around 'have' marks a direct, personal relationship.
C'est un peu tendu avec Colette.
'It is a bit tense with Colette.' Andrea confides that things are difficult at home. The descriptive adjective for 'tense' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
Sans Colette, tu veux dire.
'Without Colette, you mean.' Andrea acknowledges with bitter irony that Colette has walked out. Andrea uses the casual singular 'you' with 'mean', showing close familiarity.
José? Comment tu vas?

'Jose? How are you?' Laurence suddenly interrupts the agents with an affectionate greeting. In everyday spoken French, rising intonation on 'are doing' at the end is enough to turn the sentence into a question.
Ça fait vraiment une éternité!
'It has truly been ages!' Laurence highlights how many years have elapsed since their last encounter. Notice how 'makes' leads directly into the noun meaning 'eternity'.
Je suis ravie d'être sur ce tournage.
'I am delighted to be on this shoot.' Laurence expresses genuine joy at joining the film cast. The adjective meaning 'delighted' takes its feminine form here to match the noun it describes.
À tout à l'heure sur le plateau.
'See you shortly on the movie set.' Laurence smiles politely before heading to the dressing rooms. The key noun here means 'hour', anchored by its matching French article.
Laurence... Que fait-elle ici?
'Laurence... What is she doing here?' Jose remains petrified by the unexpected arrival of his ex-partner. Inverting the verb and pronoun around 'makes' creates a crisp, polished question.
Tu la connais depuis longtemps?

'Have you known her for a long time?' Andrea asks Jose about the history behind his shock. The informal 'you' form around 'know' marks a direct, personal relationship. Now let's listen to the full exchange once more from start to finish.
